body:
Coordinator lesson (Termal::Fable2, 2026-10-09 06:08Z; the second occurrence today). Implementers sometimes end a turn waiting for my wake without mailing me: their final text goes only to their own transcript. I wake only on mail, so the pair waits on each other. Today Opus3 sat idle about 45 min after its credited 1b check, and CSharpProof about 70 min after witness (c); earlier, CSharpProof waited about 44 min after its FAIL run. Practice: when an expected report is overdue past the step's normal length, do ONE read of termal_list_sessions (status and preview; this is a read, not polling), and wake any idle worker whose preview shows a finished step. Every wake I send asks the worker to mail me one line whenever it ends a turn waiting on me.

Seen again, 2026-10-12 02:24-02:55Z (Fable2): Termal::Merger committed w-cfcf (9836a6bd) and said "I'll request acceptance evaluation in the next turn", then idled about 30 min, because no wake arrived. Rule: whenever a worker says "next turn", send it a one-line wake right away, or within a few minutes, after any commit, freeze or naming turn.

2026-10-13 22:12Z, third Merger missed wake today (w-ae2c). The Merger wrote its holder note at 21:33:26Z and ended the turn WITHOUT mailing me; the host credited the record at 21:33:31Z. I noticed only at 22:11Z, when Engram asked whether a TermAl gate was ready: 38 minutes lost.

MECHANISM: after I send a "holder note first, then END" instruction, the Merger usually stays silent. On the very next event of ANY kind, read the item's history (show --history). If a holder note and typed_evidence_added are present, send the commit WAKE at once. Apply the same check after the commit wake, before the evaluation wake.

2026-10-14 02:49Z, again: the Merger named the w-254ae root at 02:04Z (effective next turn) and ended without mailing me. It sat idle about 45 min until I checked the item when Engram asked whether a TermAl gate was ready.

RULE ADDITION: after giving the Merger a "next package" instruction, check that item's history at my next event. A naming checkpoint with no mail means it needs a wake. Also tell the Merger in each instruction: "MAIL me whenever you end a turn waiting for a wake."

2026-10-14 21:32Z, a third occurrence that cost about 35 minutes. The Merger set the w-c538 focus in its separate final turn at 20:58Z, then went idle without mailing READY. Its READY only came at 21:32Z, after Greg noticed everyone was idle. Lesson: when I ask a worker for "focus in a separate FINAL turn, then READY", that final turn cannot be followed by another turn unless something wakes it. So either have READY mailed IN that final focus turn (it is a mailbox send, not a tracker write), or check the worker's session preview in list_sessions within about 5 minutes of the expected READY. Never just end my turn and wait on a READY that has no wake path.

2026-10-15 22:11Z, again, my own miss. After the w-63d2 gate PASS at 21:10Z I told Opus2 "1. Capture: end a turn focused on w-63d2 ... 2. In a later turn, request the evaluation", and then never sent the evaluation-turn wake. Opus2 sat idle about 60 minutes. This delayed w-63d2's landing and the train-2 carry behind it. RULE: whenever my instruction contains "in a later turn", I own the wake. Either ask the worker to mail me at the end of the capture turn and wake it at once, or check its session preview within about 5 minutes of the expected capture.

Occurrence (2026-10-16 06:21Z, my own miss, which Greg caught from the live UI). After a worker's credited run ends its turn for the host record, the NEXT step needs MY wake. The train-3a Merger ran w-a776's B-run at 05:59Z and then sat idle for 20 minutes, because I never sent the wake. That stalled the P0 landing, which was stacked on train-3a. RULE: whenever a worker reports a run or ends a turn awaiting a record, send its wake in the SAME turn I process that report, or ask the worker to mail "B DONE" after each run. Never assume an idle worker continues by itself.

Counter-lesson (2026-10-16 17:45Z). "durableButNotWoken" does NOT mean the worker is gone. I reassigned w-9b21 from Sol-edfd to Sol-a7bb within a minute; Sol-edfd had woken and claimed it, released it on my "disregard", and I then had to say "keep it". Three messages of churn. RULE: after durableButNotWoken, wait one real cycle (about 5 minutes, or the next mailbox event) before reassigning, and never reassign while the first worker's mailbox shows it active (queuedBehindActiveTurn).
